title: Pro-étale trace and its integral image on a splitting
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$ and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with its $\ell$-adic topology and valuation ring $A=\mathcal O_E$ with the subspace topology [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. For each scheme $T$ [def-pc-scheme], use its small pro-étale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], continuous coefficient ring sheaves $A_T(U)=C(|U|,A)$ and $E_T(U)=C(|U|,E)$ [def-weil-pbc-continuous-integral-coefficients], and sheaves of modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $p:V\to S$ be a finite étale scheme morphism [def-weil-pbc-finite-etale-category], let $L$ be an $E_S$-module, and let $M\subseteq p^*L$ be an $A_V$-submodule. Here inverse image is canonical coefficient pullback [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image], and $p_*$ is direct image of sheaves, evaluated by $p_*F(U)=F(V\times_SU)$. There is a unique $E_S$-linear map $\operatorname{Tr}:p_*p^*L\to L$ whose restriction to every étale splitting $V\times_SU\cong\coprod_{j\in J}U$ is $(s_j)\mapsto\sum_js_j$. Define $N\subseteq L$ as the sheaf image of $p_*M\to p_*p^*L\xrightarrow{\operatorname{Tr}}L$, that is, sections locally represented by traces of sections of $p_*M$. Then $N$ is an $A_S$-submodule, and on every such splitting $N|_U=\sum_{j\in J}M_j$ as submodule sheaves of $L|_U$, where $M_j$ is the restriction of $M$ to the $j$-th sheet.

proof.text: Choose the unique descended section supplied by section-sum descent. Its characterization proves restriction compatibility. Use bijective sheet units to give unique coordinates for two inputs and for a scalar multiple. Addition and diagonal scalar multiplication commute with their finite sums; uniqueness of descent gives additivity and coefficient linearity. PresheafOfModules.homMk builds the trace morphism. Its local-sum formula is the characterization at the identity; the same characterization and naturality prove uniqueness among all morphisms with that formula.

Construct the pointwise image of M under any trace satisfying local sums. Its integral scalar closure follows from the coefficient inclusion and projection-precomposition commutative square. Saturate the underlying subfunctor by local membership. A common refinement proves closure under addition; restrictions and scalar closure are preserved. Mathlib Subfunctor.sheafify_isSheaf proves sheafhood. Transfer covering sieves between the equivalent small model and S.ProEt to obtain exactly TraceImageLocalRepresentatives.

On a splitting, a local trace representative has unique sheet coordinates by sheet-unit bijectivity. Restrict the submodule section to show these coordinates lie in the indicated sheet submodules, and use the local-sum formula. Conversely, glue an integral sheet tuple using the sheet-lifting lemma and apply the local-sum formula. The covering sieves are preserved, so both implications give precisely TraceImageLocalSheetSum.

split_report.summary: Construct the trace from finite étale local splittings, verify locally varying permutation invariance, glue the linear maps, and compute the integral sheaf image by local representatives. Reuse existing generic tools; no new nodes. All coefficients are continuous ring sheaves, not constant sheaves. Empty fibres, variable degree, arbitrary modules and sheaf rather than sectionwise images are covered.
split_report.blueprint: sk-lem-stratified-lattice proof, Pushing down by the trace: the definition of Tr and the image composite, and the sentence that on a splitting the trace is the sum and L_0=M_1+...+M_d. No lattice-freeness or lisseness claims are used.

tool_uses.why: Generic identification of the pro-étale slice site for a site object, used to interpret restrictions; it does not replace the trace argument.
Specifies the canonical continuous coefficient map as the adjunct of projection precomposition; its restriction is explicitly calculated as identity in step 1.
Only the generic map-gluing clause for sheaves of sets is used; all trace maps, overlap agreement, and linearity are established in this item.
Only étale implies weakly étale, allowing finite étale arrows as pro-étale site objects, is used.
Generic stability of weakly étale maps supplies fibre products in the presenting site, a hypothesis of the map-gluing lemma.
